name: Tight end seam
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 53: The seam: how a tight end gets open up the middle (and why the Giants' tight end had 127 yards)
what: The tight end seam is a pass where the tight end runs straight up the middle of the field and the quarterback throws to him 15 to 25 yards downfield.

At the snap the tight end looks like he might block, then sprints upfield. He runs past the linebacker, who only guards a short area in zone coverage, and into the open space between the two deep safeties. The quarterback throws about 2.5 to 3 seconds after the snap, before a safety can close.

Teams call it because tight ends are bigger than cornerbacks and faster than most linebackers, and because Cover 2 leaves the deep middle soft. It's a quick way to gain a big chunk of yards without throwing to the sideline.

caption: White = offense, yellow = defense: the tight end (TE) runs straight up past the linebacker into the seam between the two safeties, each guarding a deep half; the dashed white line is the throw, and yellow dashes show where the defenders drop.
spot: Watch the tight end next to the tackle: if he runs straight up the field instead of blocking and there are two safeties deep, the ball often goes to him up the middle, caught between the safeties right before one arrives.
beats: Beats Cover 2 and other zone looks with two deep safeties, where the middle of the field is open. Log it as Pass in the drill.
